title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f: X -> S, apparently smooth (first line hard to read). The page opens a section titled 'Connexions et stratifications intégrables (suite, problèmes divers)'. Its aim is to define integrability of a connection as the existence of enough local horizontal sections, rather than as vanishing curvature. It then states the characteristic-p dictionary.

(1) Definitions. Let E be a quasi-coherent O_X-module with a connection relative to S.
- E is 'trivial' if E ≅ f^*F, compatibly with connections, for some quasi-coherent F on S. Here f^*F carries its canonical connection 1⊗d.
- NB: suppose f is smooth, surjective, with geometrically connected fibres, and S has characteristic 0. Then F ↦ f^*F, from QCoh(S) to modules on X with relative connection, is fully faithful, at least for F of finite presentation. The proof amounts to f_*(O_X)^{∇} = O_S, i.e. relative H^0_dR = O_S, universally. Flatness then gives Hom_∇(f^*F, f^*F') = Hom(F, F') for finitely presented F.
- E is 'locally trivial' or 'Zariski-integrable' if it is trivial locally on (X -> S) for the Zariski topology.
- E is 'integrable' if it is trivial locally for the étale topology.
- Margin: it would be more natural to phrase things with PD-connections (PD-stratifications), which amount to the same in the smooth case.

(2) Characteristic p. Let S have characteristic p and let X/S locally admit a p-basis. For quasi-coherent E with connection, the following are claimed equivalent:
- (a) Zariski-integrable;
- (b) étale-integrable;
- (c) curvature 0 and p-curvature 0;
- (d) E is trivial relative to the Frobenius twist X^{(p/S)}, i.e. E ≅ F_{X/S}^*(G) with its canonical connection.
Moreover G ↦ F_{X/S}^*(G), from quasi-coherent modules on X^{(p/S)} (the notation '(X^{(p/S)}, O/J = 1)' is unclear) to modules on X with 'integrable' connection rel S, is an equivalence of categories. This is Cartier descent / Cartier's theorem in Katz's formulation.

The page serves the programme continued on the next page. There, integrable stratifications are built by twisting with G-torsors, and stratified bundles over a field are expected to be Tannakian, equivalent to representations of a 'generalized fundamental group' Π_1(X,x).
errors: Nonstandard terminology: 'intégrable' here means 'locally trivial (étale)', not 'curvature zero'. In char p, curvature zero alone does not give integrability in this sense; the p-curvature condition (c) is needed. This is consistent, but it clashes with the usual usage.

In the NB, full faithfulness uses that horizontal functions are exactly O_S, universally (geometrically connected fibres, characteristic 0). The finite-presentation restriction is needed for Hom to commute with f^*. This is correct as stated, with the hedges given.

The equivalence (a)⇔(d) holds globally. The descended module G is unique and glues because F_{X/S}^* is fully faithful onto connections with ψ = 0, so Zariski and étale local triviality coincide. The note gives no proof, but the claim is true (Cartier, Katz 1970 Thm 5.1).

The descriptor '(X^{(p/S)}, O_{X^{(p/S)}}/J ≃ 1)' is obscure, possibly a slip or private notation. Mathematically the target should simply be X^{(p/S)} with the relative Frobenius F_{X/S}: X -> X^{(p/S)}.

ideas.what: Defining a connection to be integrable when it is locally (Zariski/étale) of the form f^*F with canonical connection
ideas.modern_name: locally trivial / 'enough horizontal sections' connections; Frobenius-integrable
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Frobenius integrability); algebraic formulation in Grothendieck's crystals work, Katz
ideas.where_published: Spirit of 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Full faithfulness of f^* from QCoh(S) to modules with relative connection, for smooth surjective f with geometrically connected fibres in char 0
ideas.modern_name: relative H^0_dR(X/S) = O_S; pullback is fully faithful on de Rham objects

ideas.what: In char p with local p-basis: integrable ⇔ curvature 0 and p-curvature 0 ⇔ Frobenius descent; F_{X/S}^* is an equivalence onto such modules
ideas.modern_name: Cartier descent / Cartier's theorem (Katz, Nilpotent connections, Thm 5.1)
ideas.where_published: Treated in Katz 1970 and Berthelot–Ogus; Grothendieck's own published account unsure

ideas.what: Remark that PD-connections (PD-stratifications) would be the more natural framework, equivalent to connections in the smooth case
ideas.modern_name: crystals on the crystalline site ↔ integrable connections (smooth case)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean restatement of standard material: Cartier descent in Katz's form, the char-0 full faithfulness of pullback, and the PD-stratification remark. The only idiosyncrasy is defining 'intégrable' as 'locally trivial'. The more interesting Tannakian / generalized π_1 thread is on the next page, not here.
transcription_corrections: First line: the word after 'X/S' is hard to read; it may be 'schéma sur S' rather than 'lisse sur S'.
'F ↦ F^*_{X/S}(F)' should read G ↦ F_{X/S}^*(G), i.e. pullback by the relative Frobenius F_{X/S}: X -> X^{(p/S)}.
In d), the struck '[-X-]' suggests an intended 'X -> (X^{(p/S)}, ...)', i.e. trivial relative to the Frobenius morphism.
In the equivalence statement, 'Modules cohérents' is probably 'Modules qu. coh.' (the hand reads like 'Modules' / 'objets' ... 'sur X^{(p/S)'}').
Margin is better read as: 'Il serait plus naturel d'inclure certains objets des travaux avec les PD-connexions [c'est pareil dans cas lisse]', with 'inclure' and 'travaux' uncertain.
